762-about-the-department-of-electrical-a: Electrical (and Honours), Computer, and Software Co-op, all with CEAB-standard math, science, design and complementary studies, including humanities or management.
762-location: McConnell Engineering Building, Room 602, 3480 University St.
762-program-description: 134–137 credits. The principles behind computers, microelectronics, robotics, telecom and power, so you can work in any of these industries, plus social science and humanities courses.
762-required-year-0-courses-22-credits: CEGEP usually gives credit. See the page for French and IB, AP and A-Levels.
763-list-b-technical-complementaries-0-1: Not both ECSE 551 and COMP 551, ECSE 463 and 562, or ECSE 465 and 565. Some are taught in French.
764-group-b-humanities-and-social-scienc: 6 credits; CEGEP usually gives 3. Arts at 200–300 in listed departments, not seminars, field, survey or topics courses or reserved ones, with some exclusions; or listed Management, Science and Engineering courses. Management and ENVR have limits. INTG 215 isn't open after INTG 201 and 202.
765-elective-course: 3 credits at 200+ from any department, approved by the Programs Office.
765-enhanced-power-concentration: 16–17 technical credits, for regular Electrical students only. Through the Institute for Electrical Power Engineering, funded mostly by Hydro-Québec, with a full final-year program, sponsored projects and internships.
765-eligibility-criteria: Fall admission only. In the regular B.Eng., CGPA 2.5+, with ECSE 362 done or underway, able to finish within three semesters.
765-selection-criteria: Five to ten students, by CGPA and CV, possibly with an interview for the scholarship and a Hydro-Québec internship.
765-curriculum-requirements-for-selected: Normal degree requirements, with these specifics.
765-required-courses-10-credits: ECSE 458D on a practical power project, ideally at the Institute or a sponsor.
766-complementary-courses: 6–7 credits. ECSE 460, 463, 464, 465, 467, 468 and 469 are Institute-sponsored and taught at Polytechnique Montréal, some in French.
766-program-description: 138–141 credits, limited and competitive, with no first-year entry. CEGEP students enter at term three, others at term five, on grades.
Take 14+ credits each term except the final two (16+ combined), and keep CGPA 3.30.
766-required-year-0-courses-22-credits: Done before entering Honours. CEGEP usually gives credit.
767-technical-complementaries: 17–20 credits, five courses: 2 from List A, 2 at 500-level ECSE, 1 from A, B, C or 500-level.
767-list-a-technical-complementaries-wit: 8–12 credits. Not both ECSE 403 and 501, or ECSE 408 and 511.
769-program-description: 133–136 credits. Depth in computer hardware and software, in well-equipped labs, for industry or graduate study, plus social science and humanities courses.
770-list-b: 0–11 credits. Not both COMP 424 and ECSE 526, or ECSE 551 and COMP 551.
772-program-description: Designing complex software, with mandatory co-op terms, across the whole lifecycle using engineering, computer science and math.
772-required-year-0-courses-25-credits: CEGEP usually gives credit. Plus 3 credits of Natural Science from ATOC, BIOL, CHEM, EPSC, ESYS or PHYS, approved by the Office.
773-list-b: 0–11 credits. Not both COMP 350 and ECSE 343, COMP 424 and ECSE 526, or ECSE 551 and COMP 551.
776-about-the-global-engineering-program: A joint degree with CentraleSupélec: two years near Paris, then two at McGill in one of nine streams, in English, for an international cohort, tackling environmental, social and corporate challenges. Leads to industry, entrepreneurship or master's study.
776-program-description: Technical and non-technical skills: math, physics, chemistry and biology, then a stream (Breadth, Biological, Chemical, Civil, Data Science, Electrical, Entrepreneurship, Materials, Mechanical), plus humanities, business and languages, in interdisciplinary global teams.
777-global-engineering-technical-complem: 41–53 credits in the stream chosen at the end of second year, each with core courses and some with technical or sustainability complementaries.
777-stream-1-breadth: 45–48 credits: 30 from List A, 9–11 from B, 6–7 from C.
778-stream-5-data-science: 46–47 credits. One of ECSE 507, MECH 559 or 579; ECSE 526 or 551.
779-stream-7-entrepreneurship: 53 credits: 50 from List A, 3 from List B.
